title: Unified Inference: Q4 2026 Product Overview, PRD & Roadmap, Pricing and Release Notes
author: Priya Shenoy
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates the product overview, high-level PRD, design guidance, roadmap and themes, pricing/packaging notes, and release notes for Redwood's Unified Inference initiative for Q4 2026. Unified Inference is Redwood's cross-environment runtime and product experience that provides a consistent API, predictable SLAs, and cost controls across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals (Q4 2026):
- Stabilize the Unified Inference public API surface for enterprise customers with v1 feature parity across deployment modes.
- Deliver cost-control primitives (auto-batching policy UI, quantization profiles, per-route routing) in Redwood Console.
- Launch pricing tiers and migration guidance for Dedicated customers migrating from pilot to reserved capacity contracts.
- Ship Unified Inference v1.3 runtime improvements (KV cache resiliency, fallback routing) and a staged rollout with telemetry and guardrails.

Problem statement / Market context:
Many customers run hybrid inference: prototypes on Hosted, predictable workloads on Dedicated, and regulated workloads on Private. Differences in tooling, rollout semantics, and metrics cause operational friction. Customers ask for one API, one rollout model, and transparent unit economics. Unified Inference reduces time-to-production while giving platform teams the controls to meet latency and cost targets.

Success metrics (12-week milestones):
- API parity: 95% of top 10 hosted endpoints implement equivalent behavior in Dedicated and Private (observability, streaming, function-calling).
- Cost: Average per-token cost improvement of 12% for workloads using recommended batching/quantization profiles.
- Reliability: P99 latency for text-generation endpoints at < 450ms on Dedicated for 512-token queries (on committed shapes).
- Adoption: 30% of active enterprise Hosted customers adopt Dedicated or Private proof-of-concept within 3 months of GA.

Scope (in-scope):
- API surface and SDK parity across environments (text generation, chat, embeddings, function calling, streaming).
- Console UX for route-level policies: batching, caching, quantization, model routing.
- Pricing tiers and migration playbooks for Dedicated (monthly commits + burst/bucket).
- Runtime improvements: KV cache eviction policy, model-variant fallback, improved kernel selection heuristics.

Out-of-scope (this release):
- New model architecture support (e.g., non-transformer experimental models).
- Major rewrite of serving runtime. Minor perf and resiliency changes only.

Product requirements (high level):
1) API & SDK parity
- Requirement: All public endpoints available in Hosted must be callable with identical semantics in Dedicated and Private.
- Acceptance criteria: SDK unit tests exercise parity matrix; conformance tests pass in Dedicated CI.

2) Route-level policies in Console
- Requirement: Enable per-route configuration of batching window (ms), max batch tokens, caching (prefix TTL), quantization profile (int8/4/none), and fallback routing policy.
- Acceptance criteria: Console UI exposes these knobs; REST API and Terraform provider support them; e2e tests validate applied config affects runtime behavior.

3) Cost controls & recommendations
- Requirement: Provide automated suggestions for batching and quantization per-route based on 7-day traffic histograms and sample prompts.
- Acceptance criteria: Recommendation engine outputs a suggested policy and projected cost delta; customers can accept/apply through Console.

4) SLAs and telemetry
- Requirement: Documented SLOs per plan (Hosted free / Hosted paid / Dedicated committed) and exportable telemetry (per-route token counts, latency distribution, cache hit rate).
- Acceptance criteria: Dashboards and raw metrics available; alerts template created for common regressions.

Non-functional requirements:
- Security: All control API calls require RBAC checks; Private mode control plane honors KMS/HSM key bindings.
- Scalability: Control plane must handle config propagation to 5k routes within 60s.
- Backward compatibility: New route policies default to previous runtime behavior; explicit opt-in required for aggressive cost controls.

Design overview (architecture & interaction):
- Components:
  - Control Plane (Console + API + Terraform provider): stores route policies and issues policy deltas to the orchestration plane.
  - Orchestration Plane: computes routing decisions, model variants, and maintains rollout state.
  - Serving Runtime: per-GPU process implementing batching, KV-cache, quantization execution paths, and fallback logic.

- Flow (simplified):
  1. Customer creates/updates a route in Console with policy P.
  2. Control Plane validates policy and stores it in Config Store (versioned).
  3. Orchestration Plane computes target model variant and rollout plan and pushes config to runtime agents.
  4. Serving Runtime applies policy; telemetry streams back to Control Plane and metrics pipeline.

API examples (REST):
- Create route with batching and quantization (JSON payload shown inline):
  POST /api/v1/routes
  {
    "name": "product-search-embeddings",
    "model": "redwood/sea-1-7b",
    "batching": {"max_batch_tokens": 4000, "batch_window_ms": 25},
    "caching": {"prefix_ttl_seconds": 3600},
    "quantization_profile": "int8",
    "fallback_policy": "model-variant"
  }

Design decisions and tradeoffs:
- Make console defaults conservative: high-latency-sensitive routes will not be auto-quantized without explicit opt-in. Tradeoff: slower early adoption vs fewer regressions.
- Recommendation engine runs asynchronously with a confidence threshold to avoid noisy suggestions.

Data and telemetry requirements:
- Per-request telemetry: request_id, route_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, cache_hit (bool), host_region, error_code.
- Retention: 90 days for high-resolution traces; 13 months for aggregated metrics.

Roadmap and themes (Q4 2026 -> Q2 2027):
- Q4 2026 (GA for Unified Inference v1.0):
  - Console Route Policies v1 (UI + API + Terraform).
  - Runtime v1.3: KV cache resiliency, fallback routing, basic quantization support.
  - Pricing Tier: Dedicated Starter / Dedicated Standard / Dedicated Enterprise.
  - Release: staged rollout with feature flags and canary for top 20 customers.

- Q1 2027 (Stabilization & Add-ons):
  - Auto-recommendations GA.
  - Dedicated Reserved contracts documentation and migration playbook.
  - Additional observability (trace linking, per-user cost attribution).

- Q2 2027 (Optimization & Scale):
  - Dynamic batching policies based on request patterns.
  - Multi-region failover policies and cross-region model routing.
  - Pricing: introduce volume discounts and invoice-level budgeting tools.

Pricing & packaging notes (high level):
- Pricing goals: signal unit economics, provide migration path from trial to reserved capacity, and maintain competitive Hosted API rates.

Pricing tiers (Dedicated):
- Dedicated Starter: monthly commit $8k, baseline throughput 50 RPS, soft SLA (99% uptime), 10% discount on token usage compared to Hosted.
- Dedicated Standard: monthly commit $30k, baseline throughput 200 RPS, 99.9% uptime SLA, 20% discount on token usage, included 24/7 support.
- Dedicated Enterprise: custom commit, dedicated account team, custom SLAs, on-prem packaging available, volume discounts negotiated.

Billing model elements:
- Components: commit fee (capacity), overage token usage (per-token), burst bucket (short-term burstable capacity), observability retention add-ons.
- Migration credits: Customers converting a Hosted invoice to Dedicated commit within 60 days receive usage credit up to 25% of first month commit.

Migration playbook (high level):
1. Pre-engagement: collect traffic histograms, cost-per-token reports, and SLOs.
2. Sizing exercise: recommend commit level and burst bucket.
3. POC: deploy Dedicated test environment with mirrored traffic (shadow mode).
4. Cutover: staged route-by-route migration with canary and rollback scripts.
5. Post-migration review: cost report and ops runbook handover.

Release notes (Unified Inference v1.0 GA - 2026-12-01):
- New: Console Route Policies (UI + API + Terraform support) — per-route batching, caching, quantization toggles.
- New: Runtime v1.3 — KV cache resiliency improvements and model-variant fallback.
- New: Dedicated pricing tiers and migration credits.
- Improved: SDK parity across Hosted and Dedicated for generation, chat, and embeddings.
- Fixed: Several edge-case race conditions in config propagation to serving agents.

Rollout & rollout guardrails:
- Canary cohort: 20 pilot customers representing a mix of latency-sensitive and throughput workloads.
- Feature flags: console-policy-v1, runtime-fallback-v1, quantization-int8.
- Monitoring: pre-defined dashboards (per-route latency, cache-hit, model-variant fallback counts) and automated alerting thresholds.
- Rollback: config reversion endpoint to revert last applied policy within 15 minutes; runtime restart is rarely required.

Operational runbook (summary):
- Ownership: Product (Priya Shenoy) owns roadmap and tradeoffs; Eng (Evan Martinez) owns runtime delivery; Eng SRE (Lina Zhang) owns rollout and SLOs.
- On-call triggers: P99 latency > target for 10 minutes, cache-hit rate drop > 30% from baseline, or spike in fallback-rate indicating model incompatibility.
- Quick mitigation steps:
  1. Validate control-plane to agent connectivity (kubectl/agent logs).
  2. Revert recent policy changes for affected route.
  3. Temporarily route traffic to hosted fallback model.
  4. Engage runtime and model-ops to investigate quantization regressions.

Open risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Quantization introduces output-quality regressions for some tasks.
  - Mitigation: Quality gate in Console requiring evaluation against a customer prompt set; allow rollbacks.
- Risk: Misconfigured batching causing increased latency for single-request flows.
  - Mitigation: Conservative defaults and per-route SLA awareness.
